records.text:
1. Opus is an open-source, low-latency audio compression format designed for real-time communication. It efficiently compresses audio data while maintaining high quality, making it ideal for voice calls and live streaming. Opus supports variable bitrates and adapts to network conditions, ensuring consistent performance across bandwidths. It is widely used in VoIP, gaming, and streaming applications.
2. Audio codecs compress audio data to reduce file size for storage or transmission. Common codecs include MP3 (balanced quality and compatibility), AAC (superior quality at similar bitrates), FLAC (lossless compression), and Opus (high efficiency in real-time use). Each has trade-offs: MP3 and AAC prioritize compatibility, FLAC preserves original quality, and Opus excels in dynamic, real-time environments with minimal latency.
